decided_by: §10 branch 1 (0 of 10 cases with a decision-path P3)

safety_metrics.comparison_note: §12 specifies these as Guard-vs-Baseline deltas. Only the baseline arm ran, so the table is a description of one arm and no delta column is reported -- a single column presented under a two-arm heading is how an absent comparison looks like a null one.

observed.note: the block contains no P3 node at all -- not one used in reasoning and not one left unused

how_surprising.reading: roughly a 6% chance under the historical rate. Low enough to say this block is quieter than the corpus it was drawn from, and not low enough to say the risk has gone. Both readings are available and this stage takes neither: what it can say is that ten cases did not exercise the guard, which is what §10 asks.

density.what_this_does_not_mean: It is not evidence that ATGG does not work. The trigger rule was shown to fire on the §9.2 controls; there was simply no P3 in this block for it to fire on. A guard that is never asked is not a guard that failed.

overhead.token_note: §12.2: the guard makes one extra LLM call per trigger and this arm had no triggers, so the marginal cost of the guard is unmeasured here; the API does not report usage per call, so no estimate is given
overhead.wall_clock_note: §12.2: reported as an engineering figure only; network variance dominates it

leakage.gold_note: case 60-69's gold is unread. §11 conditions outcome verification on both arms; with one arm the baseline's outcome is not needed by any part of §10's decision, and leaving it unread keeps the block available if the review re-scopes it.
